ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
You carry out an experiment to study transpiration in plants using a two-week-old bean plant. You set up a potometer by cutting the stem of a plant and securing it into clear flexible tubing that has been tightly connected to a calibrated pipette. Water fills the potometer from the plant stem to the tip of the pipette.

You measure water loss from your potometer at 10-minute intervals and plot your data on the graph as Line B.
You then explore what happens if you expose the plant to different conditions. Which of the following statements is correct based on proposed changes to the potometer?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Painting the upper leaf surface of most of the leaves with clear nail polish will decrease the rate of transpiration and account for Line C.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: You carry out an experiment to study transpiration in plants using a two-week-old bean plant. You set up a potometer by cutting the stem of a plant and securing it into clear flexible tubing that has been tightly connected to a calibrated pipette. Water fills the potometer from the plant stem to the tip of the pipette. You measure water loss from your potometer at 10-minute intervals and plot your data on the graph as Line B. If you paint the upper leaf surface of most of the leaves with clear nail polish, how would the rate of transpiration change, and which line on the graph would this correspond to?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Painting the upper leaf surface of most of the leaves with clear nail polish will decrease the rate of transpiration and account for Line C.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached graph has Time on the x-axis and Transpiration on the y-axis. Three lines start near the origin: Line A has the steepest positive slope, Line B has an intermediate positive slope, and Line C has the shallowest positive slope. Reasoning: The experiment’s original water-loss data are plotted as Line B. Painting the upper leaf surface of most leaves with clear nail polish would seal/block leaf surface pores such as stomata and reduce evaporation of water from the leaves. Since a lower transpiration rate means a smaller slope than Line B on the graph, the changed condition corresponds to Line C.
